    "textPayload": "    message: \"<expr type=\\\"expression\\\" label=\\\"neutral\\\"/> That's a great observation. <expr type=\\\"break\\\" label=\\\"500ms\\\"/> To answer your question, <expr type=\\\"expression\\\" label=\\\"confident\\\"/> no, you generally can't do zero percent down with a conventional loan. <expr type=\\\"break\\\" label=\\\"300ms\\\"/> Conventional loans typically require a down payment, and as you've seen, they also carry mortgage insurance if you put down less than twenty percent. <expr type=\\\"break\\\" label=\\\"1s\\\"/> <expr type=\\\"expression\\\" label=\\\"happy\\\"/> Since you have military service, switching to the VA tab is the way to explore that no-money-down option. <expr type=\\\"break\\\" label=\\\"500ms\\\"/> If you've switched to the VA tab, you should notice the mortgage insurance line has dropped to zero — VA loans don't carry monthly PMI. <expr type=\\\"break\\\" label=\\\"1s\\\"/> <expr type=\\\"expression\\\" label=\\\"curious\\\"/> What do you see on your end — does anything look different?\"",
    "insertId": "invamqu4r7g7b26h",
    "resource": {
